entries.title: Import a Google Drive folder, style clips with a look editor, create speaker kits, and re-assign sessions on clips and recordings
entries.summary: Several new capabilities land in the Media and Clips areas. **Discover → Google Drive** now lets you browse or paste a link to import an entire folder: each file is marked as new, already in your library, or a copy, and you can pick an event to preview matched sessions before importing. An **Import status** page and dock row track progress, with "Already in your library" links for duplicates. On the **Clip** page, a **Look** editor controls logo position, automatic light/dark logo selection, and captions, with a **Re-render** action; the **N clips rendering** filter and a dock row track render state across reloads, with **Try again** on failures. **Share with advocates → Each speaker, their clips** shows a speaker-kit preview of who receives what before the campaign is created. Selecting multiple clips in the library sends them all to a team campaign, giving each its own post in the wizard. A **Re-assign** control on clips and recordings lets you change the session and speakers, and asks whether to carry the change to the recording or its clips when the two sides differ.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Media / Clips

entries.use_case: A marketing team that recorded a multi-day festival can pull an entire Google Drive folder into their library in one step, style each clip with their brand logo and captions, send every speaker their own personalised clip kit, and push a batch of clips straight into a team campaign — all without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Multiple large surface areas ship together (Drive folder import, clip look editor, speaker kits, re-assign, render dock). Walk through each with the customer before they go live to confirm their Google Drive connection and brand kit are set up.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to get festival or conference footage into Sessionboard quickly, or when they want to send personalised clip kits to speakers after an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the Media and Clips features enabled who produce post-event content at scale, especially those storing recordings in Google Drive.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Discover → Google Drive; Marketing → Media → Clips
internal.gotchas: Gallery, course and team-campaign actions on the clip page are shown only when the org has those products enabled. 'Send to team campaign' replaces any Dispatch naming visible to the customer — do not refer to it as Dispatch in customer-facing conversations.
internal.talk_track: After your event wraps, point Sessionboard at your Google Drive folder and it will match every file to the right session. From there you can style clips with your logo and captions, preview exactly which clips each speaker will receive, and launch a team campaign so your whole team posts on the same day.

draft.docs_gap: The media-library guide should add a section on Google Drive folder import (browsing, pasting a link, file status indicators, the import status page and dock row) and the clips guide should add sections on the Look editor, render state tracking, speaker kits, multi-clip team campaigns, and the Re-assign control.
draft.why_use_it: Media and Clips turn your event recordings into ready-to-share content. Import footage from Google Drive or other sources, let Sessionboard match files to sessions and speakers automatically, then generate branded clips with captions and your logo. Share clips directly with speakers through Advocacy or push them to your team as a Dispatch campaign so everyone posts on the same day.

entries.title: Write Swoogo Registration IDs back to Sessionboard contacts
entries.summary: A new Swoogo event setting, **Write back Swoogo Registration ID to contacts**, makes each sync read the mapped Swoogo event's registrants and write each registrant's ID to the matching contact of the Sessionboard event. Contacts are matched by the ID they already hold, then by email (ignoring capitals and spaces). The ID goes to a read-only **Swoogo Registration ID** contact field created when you turn the setting on, or to a text contact field you pick. Unmatched and ambiguous registrants are listed in the sync log. Off by default, per event mapping.

enable.path: Org Settings → Integrations → Swoogo → Event Settings → Write back Swoogo Registration ID to contacts

where.path: Event → Contacts → Swoogo Registration ID field

entries.use_case: An organizer whose attendees register in Swoogo can see on each speaker's contact whether that person is registered, and reference the registrant record, without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Off by default. The customer turns it on per event mapping in the Swoogo event settings.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A Swoogo customer asks which of their speakers or contacts have registered, or wants the Swoogo registrant ID on the contact (LegalTechTalk asked first, SB-11078).
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the Swoogo integration connected whose speakers also register in Swoogo.
internal.gotchas: Registrants never create contacts. Two contacts sharing one email, or two registrants matching one contact, are skipped. Reading the registrant list counts toward Swoogo's API rate limit; a 429 stops the sync.
